plan.name: Discover Python components with stable source identities
plan.summary: Extend project.ResolveComponents and project.Load to inventory explicit Python scopes without recursion, retaining every non-test source file and named synchronous, asynchronous, decorated and nested function or qualified method, with deterministic ordinals for repeated declarations and no assurance claims. Use isolated Python 3 standard-library syntax parsing without importing or executing inspected code, provide that parser runtime in the plumbing sandbox, and resolve targets, supported inline Nagini contracts, tests and conformance references exactly once with the existing path containment, sorted snapshots and separate input provenance. Python IDs use the project-relative dotted source module (including __init__), lexical symbol and source path; source hashes cover complete files, while contract hashes cover the concatenated exact expression bytes of direct standalone Requires, Ensures, Exsures and Decreases calls in their owning function, independently of bodies, surrounding comments and the +nagini marker. Preserve all Go identities and omitted-components behavior, reject unsupported explicit TypeScript discovery and unsupported selections, and keep verify.ErrComponents for explicit code verification before verification tools run while allowing model-only checking. Update SPEC.md and README.md with these identity, ordinal, supported syntax, contract-byte and parser-runtime rules and the discovery-only execution limit, citing D-0023, D-0024, D-0031, D-0152, D-0158 and D-0122 as applicable; the merger must record the new Python identity and contract-hashing rules and cite that decision in SPEC.md, with decision recording and unavailable Docker or network checks left as Merger work and ratified statements and locks untouched.

tests.name: TestPythonDiscoveryInventoriesSyntaxWithoutExecution
tests.says: Every scoped non-test Python source and named declaration is inventoried, including async, decorated and nested declarations; strings, comments, lambdas, subdirectories and test files add no production components and inspected code never executes.

tests.name: TestPythonDiscoveryResolvesSelectionsAndProvenance
tests.says: Qualified targets and contracts resolve in scope, Python tests and drivers may resolve elsewhere in the project, and canonical source snapshots, assumptions and inert invocations remain separate provenance without assurance.

tests.name: TestPythonDiscoveryIDsAndHashesAreIndependent
tests.says: Relocation, host import paths and configuration reordering preserve the entire inventory; line and body edits preserve IDs and contracts but change source hashes, while contract edits change only the owning contract hash.

tests.name: TestPythonDiscoveryNumbersRepeatedLexicalDeclarations
tests.says: Repeated functions, methods and containing classes get selectable lexical ordinals, including nested descendants; bare ambiguous names fail and declaration reordering can change an ordinal's selected source contract.

tests.name: TestPythonDiscoveryHashesOnlySupportedContractBytes
tests.says: Only supported direct standalone Nagini calls contribute exact original expression bytes in source order, including multiline and CRLF bytes; markers, strings, comments, nested bodies and unsupported qualified or alias forms are not contracts.

tests.name: TestPythonDiscoveryRejectsInvalidSourceAndSelections
tests.says: Valid Python manifests load, but malformed scoped or selected source, missing or duplicate references, empty or invalid contracts, out-of-scope targets and unsupported selected forms fail with useful diagnostics.

tests.name: TestPythonDiscoveryContainsEveryInputPath
tests.says: Python scopes, source selections, assumptions and invocation inputs and directories reject unclean paths and symbolic links, including escapes and links pointing inside the project.

tests.name: TestPythonDiscoveryPreservesGoAndLegacyIdentities
tests.says: Python discovery coexists with unchanged Go IDs and contract hashes, omitted-components metadata-only loading in every existing language, and explicit TypeScript rejection without rewriting manifests or locks.

tests.name: TestExplicitPythonDiscoveryStillRefusesCodeVerification
tests.says: After a valid explicit Python manifest loads, Check and Run return verify.ErrComponents without starting verification tools or executing project code; model-only and omitted-components legacy paths still reach their existing tools.
